newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN investigates violence against SAfrican women.
newsitem.headline: UN investigates violence against SAfrican women.

text.p: The United Nations special investigator into violence against women began a week-long mission to South Africa on Thursday to look into allegations of widespread rape and how the government was combating it.

Radhika Coomaraswamy, a Sri Lankan lawyer and human rights activist, will meet senior government officials including Foreign Affairs Minister Alfred Nzo and Justice Minister Dullah Omar, according to a U.N. statement issued in Geneva.
She will also discuss the issue with non-governmental organisations, women's groups and female victims of violence.
Stops are planned in Pretoria, Johannesburg and Cape Town.

As part of her three-year mandate from the U.N. Human Rights Commission, which began in April 1994, Coomaraswamy carries out fact-finding missions worldwide to study violence against women in the family, the community and as perpetrated by the state.
She is due to present a report with recommendations on her South African visit to the 53-member Commission at its next annual meeting being held in Geneva from March-April 1997.

Previous missions were carried out to South Korea and Japan on the issue of military sexual slavery during World War Two, to Poland concerning trafficking and forced prostitution of women in Eastern Europe, and to Brazil regarding domestic violence.
